h1: The 6 Best Portable Hose Reel Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Portable Hose Reel Carts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 portable hose reel carts scored on hose capacity, wheel size, frame material, stability and how much assembly each one needs.
summary: The Giraffe Tools cart is our top portable hose reel: a low center of gravity, a solid brass connector and a choice of 150 ft of 5/8 inch or 200 ft of 1/2 inch hose. GrillTown's Hosemobile is the easiest to start with because it arrives assembled with a watertight Easylink connection. VEVOR's steel cart is the sturdy budget pick, and the Yestar suits shorter hoses and different heights.
intro: Hose reel carts look interchangeable until you tip one over. A full 5/8 inch hose is heavy, and almost all of that weight sits high on the reel, so a cart with a high center of gravity falls forward the moment you pull the handle past vertical. That, not capacity, is the real dividing line in this category.

We reviewed six two-wheeled portable carts from their specs, weighing stability and hose capacity first, then frame material, wheel size and assembly. Most hold 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose. Hose itself is rarely included, and the listings do not agree on what counts as a lead-in, so read the box contents before you order.

products.name: Giraffe Tools 200 ft Hose Reel Cart 1/2 Inch
products.verdict: Low center of gravity, brass hardware and a two-hose capacity rule make it the most stable.
products.description:
The Giraffe holds 150 ft of 5/8 inch hose or 200 ft of 1/2 inch hose on a powder-coated metal frame with a low center of gravity, a solid brass connector and a 5 ft lead-in hose. It ships mostly pre-assembled.

The low stance is why it beats the 175 ft resin carts: with the reel closer to the axle, a full reel resists tipping when you tilt the cart. Its capacity is the lowest for 5/8 inch hose, 150 ft against 175, a real tradeoff.

Buy it if you roll a long hose across a sloped yard. The caveat is the price, the highest here, and 150 ft of 5/8 inch limits reach versus the 175 ft models.

products.name: GrillTown Hosemobile 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: Arrives fully assembled with a watertight Easylink connection and a sturdy resin build.
products.description:
The Hosemobile holds 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose, comes fully assembled, uses sturdy resin construction and measures 22 w x 45 h x 22.8 l inches. Its Easylink connection is described as watertight.

The assembled arrival is the draw, since poorly aligned reels are a common cause of leaks. It ranks below the Giraffe because the listing says nothing about center of gravity, and 45 inches tall is a tall reel to tip. It ranks above VEVOR for resin that will not rust.

Choose it if you do not want to build anything. The caveat is that resin flexes more than steel under a full load.

products.idealFor: Buyers who want a cart working in five minutes.

products.name: VEVOR 175 ft Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: A heavy-duty steel frame and solid PVC wheels for a rugged yard cart.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose on a heavy-duty steel frame with two solid PVC wheels and a non-slip handle. The listing states that no hose is included.

Steel is stiffer than the resin carts, so the reel does not rock when fully loaded. Solid wheels never go flat, which is its advantage over any pneumatic option. It lands third because the listing gives no dimensions or assembly details, which the GrillTown does.

It suits a rough lawn and storage in a shed. The caveat is rust: steel needs a dry spot, and solid wheels ride harder over roots.
products.idealFor: Rough yards where a rigid frame beats resin.
products.skipIf: You store the cart outdoors all year.

products.name: Yestar Portable Hose Reel Cart With Adjustable Handrail
products.verdict: An adjustable handrail and quick 10 minute assembly for 75 to 150 ft of hose.
products.description:
The Yestar takes 75 to 150 ft of 5/8 inch hose, has an adjustable handrail set with a carabiner, a powder-coated frame with aluminum tube support and about 10 minutes of assembly.

The adjustable handrail suits households where the person pulling the cart differs in height, which is a real ergonomics benefit that no 175 ft cart here offers. It ranks fourth because the 150 ft ceiling is lower than the 175 ft models.

It works for smaller yards and mixed-height households. The caveat is the capacity range: many buyers own 100 to 150 ft hoses, so check yours first.
products.idealFor: Smaller yards or shared use by people of different heights.
products.skipIf: You own a hose over 150 ft.

products.name: 175 ft Compact Resin 2-Wheel Hose Reel Cart
products.verdict: A weather-resistant resin cart with a metal frame and 7 inch wheels at about 24 x 20 x 32 in.
products.description:
This cart holds 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose and measures about 24 x 20 x 32 inches. Resin construction is paired with a metal frame, and the two wheels are 7 inches.

At 32 inches tall it is the shortest reel here, a lower stance than the 45 inch GrillTown. It ranks fifth since the listing says nothing about connector material or lead-in hose, both of which the Giraffe spells out.

Choose it where storage space is tight. The caveat is that 7 inch wheels sink in soft soil more than larger wheels would.
products.skipIf: Your yard is soft or uneven.

products.name: 175 ft Portable Hose Reel Cart With 7 Inch Wheels
products.verdict: The lowest-priced cart, fully assembled with a leader hose and 7 inch wheels.
products.description:
This resin cart holds 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose, arrives fully assembled, and includes a leader hose with 7 inch wheels. It is weather-resistant.

The included leader hose and assembled arrival make it the lowest-effort cart, and it undercuts every other resin model. It ranks last because the listing gives no dimensions, frame details or connector material, so you buy on faith.

It suits renters and light-duty watering. The caveat is that the missing specs leave durability unproven.

whatMatters.detail: A loaded reel is top-heavy, so a cart tips forward when you tilt it past vertical. A low stance, with the reel closer to the axle, resists that. Look for the phrase low center of gravity, or compare heights: a 32 inch cart is steadier than a 45 inch one.

Capacity depends on hose diameter. 175 ft of 5/8 inch fits the same reel as roughly 200 ft of 1/2 inch hose. Check which diameter the listing uses, and measure your own hose before ordering, because a reel that is too small overflows and tangles.

Steel is stiff but can rust, resin resists weather but flexes, and powder-coated metal sits between. Match the material to storage: a shed favors steel, while a cart that lives outdoors favors resin. Scan the listing for coating or weather-resistant wording, and be wary of listings that name no material at all, because a vague frame description usually hides thin tubing.

Larger wheels roll over roots and soft ground better than 7 inch ones, and solid wheels never go flat but ride rougher than pneumatic tires. Check diameter and tire type on the listing, and favor bigger wheels if your lawn is uneven or sloped.

The brass or plastic connector at the reel is the most common leak point. Solid brass lasts longer than plastic. A lead-in hose links the reel to the spigot, and listings differ on whether one is included. Confirm both before you buy, and expect to add thread tape or a spare washer the first season, since even good connectors weep a little until they seat.

faq.q: Do these carts include a hose?
faq.a: Not usually. The VEVOR states hose is not included, and the Giraffe and the 7 inch wheel cart include only a short lead-in or leader hose. Plan on buying the main hose separately.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring hose diameter. A reel rated for 175 ft of 5/8 inch hose holds a different length of 1/2 inch hose. The Giraffe lists both, 150 ft and 200 ft, so use that as your guide.

faq.q: Is the Giraffe worth it over the VEVOR?
faq.a: If you roll across slopes, yes. The Giraffe adds a low center of gravity and a brass connector, but holds 150 ft of 5/8 inch versus the VEVOR's 175 ft. On flat ground the VEVOR saves money.
The GrillTown and the 7 inch wheel cart arrive fully assembled, the Giraffe is mostly pre-assembled, and the Yestar takes about 10 minutes. The VEVOR lists no assembly detail, so allow extra time.

faq.q: How should I store a cart for winter?
faq.a: Drain the hose, release the connector and store the cart dry. Steel models like the VEVOR benefit most from a shed, while resin carts such as the GrillTown tolerate weather but still last longer indoors.

faq.q: Can I use a 100 ft hose on a 175 ft cart?
faq.a: Yes, but it sits loosely on the reel. The Yestar, rated for 75 to 150 ft, is a better fit for shorter hoses, since the others are sized around 175 ft.

finalTake: The Giraffe Tools cart is the one to buy if stability matters, thanks to its low center of gravity and brass connector. The GrillTown is the easy resin option that arrives built, and the VEVOR is the rigid steel alternative. Use the cheapest generic cart only for a flat lawn, and check your hose diameter first.
